developments.reason: Reviewed Wren's round-9 request (Cultivate meadow roots: a learnable, physically feasible way to propagate known edible meadow roots and keep a renewable patch, from four owned roots, with unknown costs, and no roots or growth from requesting or learning) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general cultivate-plants operation with modes inspect, plant, tend, inspect-progress and abandon for any learner and any physically supported propagule; inspection in one round at 0.2 energy through the probe observation path, reporting visible integrity and never viability; planting one whole owned unit per position in two active rounds at 1 energy each on shallow, loose, hand-workable soil without a tool, reserving the unit and transferring it exactly once into an identifiable plot record with its quantity, origin and condition; an empirical trial with a 20-round observation window and optional checks at rounds 5, 10 and 20, each 0.2 energy, reporting only actual changes and recording no visible change as inconclusive; growth only from a coded recipe over elapsed qualifying time with a production ledger; tending at one round and 0.5 energy per plot for inspection and removal of accessible competing growth, with no water, fertilizer or growth bonus; harvest only through gather at its existing 2 energy; and interruption, cancel, abandon and death rules that refund no energy or time. The specification is self-consistent and the existing ecology grounds propagation, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Reuse: ex16 already developed cultivate-plants@1 for the same request, and the ex17 specification fits it with small differences. long-plant-cultivation.ts now builds both packages from one factory, cultivation(variant). The ex16 variant keeps its id, scope long-ex16, handler long.cultivate-plants, 1.5-energy rounds, modes plant/tend/inspect/end, texts and events. Its serialized package is byte-identical to before; ex16 replay compatibility, ex7-ex15 replay compatibility and the three ex16 test files are unchanged and pass. The ex17 variant is a new package, plant-cultivation@1, in scope long-ex17, with handler long.plant-cultivation and equivalence cultivation:plant-propagule:trial-inspect-tend:1 (learning 3; the ability serializes to 3,473 code units, within the 3,500 limit). Its package id differs because package keys and handler ids must be unique across the registry. Further reuse: ex15 cultivation-trial@1's law constants, treated-unit list, ageing, plant, observation-input, footprint and reach helpers through its existing exports; its cultivation-trial drawing (visualComponents ['cultivation-trial']); the unchanged open-ecology.ts establishment, growth, dispersal and spacing law; forest-environment.ts ageing; long-planting-site.ts; collective-work.ts escrow, paid work and stop; open-foundation.ts probe and personal records; and base gather. Implemented (ex17). Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) gathered from a living plant of the same food. x, y name a 0.25 m plot within reach on hand-workable ground, under the existing long-planting-site rule: ordinary meadow soil '.', no water or wet bank, waterlogging at most 0.1, clear of people and reserved objects. The site also needs local soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and fewer than 3 plants of that food or prepared plots within 5 m. Every check runs before any cost, so a refusal spends nothing and gives the observed reason. Round 1 (1 energy) escrows the unit, still carried, owned and ageing, and creates the plot (cultivation-site-prepared). Round 2 (1 energy) rechecks reach, site, unit and energy, then moves the unit with its origin, mass and age into the plot as an unowned reserved stack that cannot be eaten or used, and records its decay at transfer. The plot gets exactly the seedling data that the dispersal law gives a natural propagule (cultivation-propagule-planted; no food is created; no qualified flag, so no practice milestone). It gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture, waterlogging and season. At the existing threshold (12; 60 for woody plants) the unit is absorbed into the new plant (cultivation-plot-established). Stock then grows one unit per growth interval up to min(4, source capacity) (cultivation-crop-matured at the first unit) and is harvested only through unchanged gather. If the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies and stops growing (cultivation-trial-failed). An unworked round, too little energy, leaving reach or a changed site pauses without charge (cultivation-work-paused). Plant resumes the person's own work and pays only the remaining round (cultivation-work-resumed). Production ledger: from placement, the hidden plot data (not in public fields or event metadata) records accounted rounds, qualifying rounds with positive growth, establishment, post-establishment growth, units produced and units removed by gather, foraging or dispersal; stock always equals produced minus removed, and a dead plot accounts no further rounds. Inspect (one round, 0.2 energy): with inputStackId, it checks one owned unreserved unit and reports resource, quantity, origin, harvest tick, decay, condition (1 - decay/lifetime), represented treatments, buds 'not represented', viability 'unknown', and whether it can be planted with the exact refusal reason. With x, y as well, it applies the exact plant site check at a site within reach and reports ground, moisture, waterlogging, regime and the reason. Nothing is consumed or reserved; this is an unverified personal record (cultivation-condition-observed, scope unit). With target, a plant source or plot in reach is observed through the baseline probe, as in ex16. Inspect-progress (target a plot in reach; one round, 0.2 energy through the baseline probe) compares lifecycle, stage, visible stock and sprouted with the same person's previous plot record, or with the covered state at placement. It returns 'changed' with each field's before and after, or 'inconclusive', and reports the window (20 rounds, endsAt, open, nextCheck among 5, 10, 20) as an unverified record (cultivation-condition-observed, scope plot). Tend (target a planted or sprouted plot in reach; any learner; one round, 0.5 energy) records the same visible-state observation and checks the 0.6 m clearance for competing plants (cultivation-plot-tended, with competingPlants and removed 0); it adds no water, nutrient or growth, and a tended plot establishes exactly like an untended control. Abandon (one round, no energy) acts only on the person's own unfinished planting and returns the unit once in its current condition. It clears the empty site (cultivation-trial-ended); after placement it is refused at no cost, and the plot and unit stay. Death before placement stops the work and leaves the unit, unowned, where the person died (cultivation-trial-failed); a placed unit stays planted. Nothing is refunded. Differences from the specification and modeling assumptions. (1) The species and material recipe is the existing general plant law, not a meadow-root botany model. Viable input: a whole untreated unspoiled unit from a living plant of the same food. Environmental ranges: planting moisture 0.3-1.2, and growth driven by temperature (root minimum 3, optimum 16), light, soil and climate moisture, waterlogging and season. Rooting: establishment 12 accumulated growth, so its duration depends on conditions and no fixed date is promised. Survival and decay: the buried unit keeps its food ageing (root lifetime 240), and spoiling kills the plot. Harvestable mass: stock units times resource mass (root 0.4). Retained living structure: the plant object itself, which gather never removes, so complete destructive harvest is not an available operation and renewal continues. Regeneration interval: the source plant's interval. Carrying capacity: min(4, source capacity). The same law applies to every food with a growth cycle and an ageing lifetime. (2) Water and nutrients exist in that law only as rate factors (soil moisture, climate moisture, waterlogging, depletion), not as stocks a plant consumes. The ledger therefore records production and losses but debits no pool, because adding a pool only for planted plots would make them grow differently from natural seedlings under the same law. (3) Quantity is 1 per plant action: each further unit needs its own plot, input and full cost, so the four roots are never spent automatically. (4) Shoots and buds are not represented on harvested units, so inspection says so instead of reporting them. (5) Competing growth: the existing rules start no plant within 0.6 m of another object, and growth does not depend on neighbors, so no competing growth can stand in a plot's clearance. Physical removal is therefore not implemented: a plant found there through some other rule is reported and left in place. (6) Inspections are allowed at any time; the 20-round window and its checks at 5, 10 and 20 are reported as a schedule and change nothing. (7) Unit and site inspection spend the 0.2 observation cost directly rather than calling the probe, because the probe's observe mode on a carried stack records only the person's own soil; plant sources and plots use the probe itself. (8) Retrieving a placed unit is not supported, as the specification allows. (9) The specification's proposed stages map to preparing, planted (no sprout seen), established (sprouted, with harvestable stock in the drawing), dead and ended. 'Stressed' is not a separate stage: stalled growth shows only as unchanged visible state. (10) Death leaves unplaced material on the ground where the person died, because the world has no estate. (11) No satisfaction, pleasure or comfort source is added: the review's optional bounded practice and information benefits are not required by the specification and were left out. Records are unverified, so the existing information-gain rule applies only through the probe's own dated-change rule. (12) Hand work needs no tool and is limited to ordinary soil; forest floor, dry hard ground and wet ground are refused. Soil moisture is read locally at the site, not taken from the reported 0.65. At Wren's current position the ground is forest floor, so planting there is refused at no cost. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex17-plant-cultivation.test.ts) cover scope separation from ex16, unique handlers, the size limit and excluded vocabulary, learning, the two 1-energy rounds, conservation, the hidden ledger, establishment equal to a natural control seedling, absorption, ledger accounting through stock and gather, rot failure and the inconclusive and changed progress looks, cost-free refusals, unit and site inspection without consumption, tending at 0.5 energy without growth change by another learner, a reported but unremoved plant in the clearance, pause, resume and planter-only abandon, another food (berry) and death.
